accuracy.evidence: Curriculum wording checked against Development Matters 2023 PSED for 3 and 4-year-olds ('develop their sense of responsibility and membership of a community', 'be increasingly independent in meeting their own care needs') and the EYFS 2024 Managing Self early learning goal. Pet facts follow PDSA and RSPCA guidance that chocolate, grapes and raisins are poisonous to dogs; the 'grown-up job' set (sharp knives, hot pans, heavy loads, kettles) follows RoSPA under-fives kitchen safety advice. The cup step is genuine one-to-one correspondence.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the real early-years slips: hiding toys counts as tidy (the Under sofa box is refused with 'Hidden is not tidy'), tidying is only a grown-up's job (challenge tag 'adult'), giving a second cup to someone who already has one (refused: 'Mum has a cup already. One cup for each person'), sharing human treats with a dog (chocolate refused), and choosing jobs that are too heavy, sharp or hot (heaviest bag and sharp knife refused with a right-sized alternative).

lab_distinct.evidence: The mechanism is household contribution: a four-home put-away sort with a refused hiding place, a floor-path where Teddy trips on the first toy left lying until every toy is collected, a one-cup-per-seat table, a pet bowl that only accepts dog food and water, and scene-based offers of help. It shares no task with flaghelp (asking for help) or flagbrave, and the 30% shingle gate passed against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds out by doing: tapping Walk with toys down makes Teddy trip on the car and names it, so the reason for tidying is experienced before the step text says 'We tidy up so no one trips'; dropping the coat in the toy box names its real home; a second cup on Mum is refused; chocolate in Pip's bowl gets 'makes dogs very poorly'. Each step's closing line only confirms what the task showed.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'Yes, I can not see them' (under the sofa) is disproved when the Under sofa box refuses every toy; 'Nothing at all' (toys on the floor) is disproved when Teddy trips; 'Yes, as a treat' (chocolate for Pip) is disproved when the bowl refuses it and explains why.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with twelve tagged messages that each name the slip: hiding blocks, leaving them on the floor, tidying is only for grown-ups, no reason to tidy, one cup shared by all, two cups in one place, chocolate for a dog, sweets for a dog, the sharp knife, the hot pan, walking away from a spill and laughing at a friend's spill.

readability.evidence: Kid text reads at FK 0.4 in sentences of three to ten words about blocks, books, cups and a dog; canvas words are one to five words beside large emoji; every action has a young-class 56 px button. Adult text reads at FK 5.0 while using the exact EYFS terms Personal, Social and Emotional Development, sense of responsibility and membership of a community, Managing Self and one-to-one correspondence.

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler patterns and the 12% duplicate gate (including against Asking for Help and Rules and routines lessons). Each kid paragraph adds one idea (homes for things, tripping and hiding, real jobs, right-sized jobs); the adult paragraphs give the EYFS statements, how to set tidying up, common adult mistakes with the pet-food warning, and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android light and iPhone 13 dark screenshots of all six steps: the held card and four homes in a 2x2 grid, the floor path with four toys and the door, the four seats and table, the three pet items and bowls, and the helping scene with hearts all fit with nothing clipped; buttons wrap onto rows. phone_sweep reported 0 findings.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: every task completes with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in light and dark themes, no console errors. Every drag or tap on the canvas has a button route (four home buttons, Pick up per toy and Walk, a button per person, a button per pet item, the three offers) and the canvas aria-label announces each result.
